content: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits to your health outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it is important to be aware of the following: 1. Severe Intestinal Condition: This medication may rarely cause a serious intestinal condition due to an overgrowth of a bacterium called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after the treatment has been discontinued. Symptoms may include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or cramping. If you experience these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. 2. Fungal Infections: Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. These are fungal infections that can occur when the natural balance of microorganisms in the body is disrupted. 3. Allergic Reactions: Although rare, serious allergic reactions to this medication can occur. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms. 4. Incomplete Side Effect List: The side effects mentioned here are not exhaustive. If you notice any unusual or persistent symptoms, consult your doctor or pharmacist. 5. Precautions Before Use: Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin). Also, disclose any other allergies you may have, as this product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. 6. Vaccination Interference: This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. 7. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It does not pass into breast milk, but consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 8. Drug Interactions: This medication may interact with other drugs, potentially altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 9. Lab Test Interference: This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor that you are using this medication. 10. Overdose: In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 11. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 12. Storage Instructions: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 13. Medical and Lab Appointments: While taking this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., kidney function tests) to monitor your condition. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. 14. Important Information: This document provides a summary of key information about this medication but does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. If you have any questions or concerns about this medication, do not hesitate to contact your healthcare provider.
